You are to create a complete, productionready web application called Event Access, implementing all described functionalities from the provided “Description des Fonctionnalités” document (French spec describing registration, QR code generation, admin approval, scanning, and avatar with TTS). Build this system endtoend, following every specification below exactly.



 OBJECTIVE
Deliver a fully working web application that:
 Allows users to register for an event (conference or fair)
 Generates a QR code per participant and emails it to them
 Lets admins accept/reject registrations
 Provides QR scanning (camerabased) for entry logging
 Displays a silent woman avatar video and plays a personalized TTS welcome message
 Is containerized with Docker, fully documented, and tested



 TECHNOLOGY STACK (must use these)
 Backend: Laravel 10 (PHP 8.2)
 Frontend: Angular 17 (TypeScript, RxJS, Angular CLI)
 Database: MySQL 8
 QR Code Library: simplesoftwareio/simpleqrcode
 Camera QR Scanning: @zxing/browser
 Speech/TTS: Browser Web Speech API (clientside, French by default)
 Mail: Laravel Mail with MailHog for local dev
 Auth: Laravel Sanctum (API token auth for admin routes)
 Containerization: Docker & Docker Compose v3.8
 CI/CD: GitHub Actions
 Testing: PHPUnit (backend), Jest/Vitest (frontend unit), Cypress (E2E)
 Docs: OpenAPI 3.0 spec + Markdown architecture diagrams



 ️ REPOSITORY STRUCTURE


eventaccess/
├─ backend/ (Laravel)
│ ├─ app/, routes/, migrations/, mail/, tests/
│ ├─ Dockerfile
│ └─ .env.example
├─ frontend/ (Angular)
│ ├─ src/app/components/
│ │ ├─ register/
│ │ ├─ adminlist/

│ │ └─ speakeravatar/
│ ├─ assets/avatarsilent.mp4
│ ├─ angular.json, package.json, Dockerfile
├─ dockercompose.yml
├─ Makefile
├─ docs/
│ ├─ openapi.yaml
│ ├─ architecture.md
│ └─ assumptions.md
├─ .github/workflows/ci.yml
└─ README.md





 DATABASE SCHEMA

 participants
| Column | Type | Notes |
||||
| id | bigint (auto) | Primary key |
| first_name | string(255) | required |
| last_name | string(255) | required |
| gender | enum('Homme','Femme','Autre') | required |
| phone | string(30) | nullable |
| email | string(255) | required, unique |
| access_type | enum('foire','conference','both') | required |
| qr_token | string(128) | HMACsigned |
| qr_payload | json | stored payload |
| status | enum('pending','accepted','rejected') | default 'pending' |
| created_at / updated_at | timestamps |

 scans
| Column | Type | Notes |
||||
| id | bigint | Primary key |
| participant_id | foreign key → participants.id | cascade |
| scanned_at | timestamp | |
| scanner_user | string | nullable |
| raw_payload | json | original QR data |
| created_at / updated_at | timestamps |

 admins
| Column | Type | Notes |
||||
| id | bigint | Primary key |
| name | string | |
| email | string | unique |
| password | string | bcrypt |
| api_token | string | nullable |

Seed one admin: admin@example.com / password: admin123.



 ⚙️ BACKEND (Laravel) REQUIREMENTS

 Routes (under /api/v1)
 POST /register
 Validates user input
 Creates participant (status: pending)
 Generates QR payload {id,uuid,email,access_type}
 Signs payload with HMAC_SHA256(payload, QR_HMAC_SECRET)
 Generates PNG QR (300x300)
 Stores qr_token and qr_payload
 Sends email with embedded QR (MailHog for dev)
 Returns JSON { ok:true, participant:{}, qr:<base64> }

 GET /participants (admin only)
 Lists all participants (with filters: status/access_type)

 POST /admin/participants/{id}/accept
 Marks as accepted and sends confirmation email

 POST /admin/participants/{id}/reject
 Marks as rejected

 POST /scan
 Input: { payload: "<b64payload>.<b64sig>", scanner_user?: string }
 Verifies signature using HMAC
 Rejects invalid or nonaccepted participants
 Inserts scan record
 Returns { ok:true, participant:{}, scan_id:<id> }

 POST /auth/login
 Admin login → returns Sanctum token

 GET /health
 Returns {status:"ok", db:true}

 Mail
 ParticipantAccessMail uses Blade view emails/participant_access.blade.php
 Content changes by status:
 Pending → “Votre demande d’accès est en attente”
 Accepted → “Accès confirmé — Bienvenue”
 Rejected → “Accès refusé — merci de vérifier vos informations”

 Security
 .env contains QR_HMAC_SECRET
 Ratelimit /register and /scan
 Use Sanctum token for admin routes
 CORS allows only FRONTEND_URL
 HMAC signature validation (constanttime compare)

 Logging
 Dedicated scans log channel for scan attempts
 Log invalid signatures with warning

 Tests
 PHPUnit tests: registration, validation, accept/reject, scan success/failure, auth
 Aim ≥80% coverage



 FRONTEND (Angular) REQUIREMENTS

 Pages & Components

 1. /register
 Fields: first_name, last_name, gender, phone, email, access_type
 Validations for required/email/phone
 Submit → POST /register
 Display QR image & “Email sent” message
 Provide print/download button
 Responsive and accessible

 2. /admin (Dashboard)
 Login form (email/password)
 Displays list of participants (table)
 Actions: Accept / Reject / Show QR
 Filters by status & access type
 Shows status color tags

 3. /admin/scanner
 Accesses camera using @zxing/browser
 Detects and decodes QR → POST /scan
 On success:
 Shows participant info
 Plays speaker avatar (see below)
 Logs last 10 scans (with time)

 4. SpeakerAvatarComponent
 Displays /assets/avatarsilent.mp4
 Input: name, access
 Plays TTS:
 If accepted → “Bonjour [name], vous avez un accès garanti à l’événement [access]”
 Else → “Désolé [name], votre inscription n’est pas valide.”
 Uses speechSynthesis (lang='frFR')
 Graceful fallback text if unsupported

 Technical
 Centralized ApiService for all HTTP calls
 Environment variables (environment.ts)
 French labels, i18nready structure
 Unit tests for form validation, ApiService, avatar TTS
 Cypress E2E test covering:
 Register flow
 Admin accept flow
 QR scan flow (simulate QR payload)



 QR SIGNATURE FORMAT
 Payload JSON: { "id": <id>, "uuid": "<uuid>", "email": "<email>", "access": "<access_type>" }
 Signature = HMAC_SHA256(payload, QR_HMAC_SECRET)
 Final encoded QR string = base64url(payload).base64url(signature)
 On scan: backend splits, verifies signature, decodes payload, validates participant.



 AVATAR ASSET
 Add a silent MP4 file in frontend/src/assets/avatarsilent.mp4
 Source: royaltyfree clip from [Pexels](https://pexels.com/videos) (“friendly woman greeting”)
 Fallback image: avatarsilent.jpg



 DOCKER SETUP
 dockercompose.yml
Services:
 mysql (MySQL 8)
 backend (Laravel app)
 frontend (Angular app)
 mailhog (SMTP test inbox)

Expose ports:
 backend: 8000
 frontend: 4200
 mailhog: 8025

 Makefile


make up → dockercompose up build d
make down → dockercompose down
make seed → docker exec backend php artisan db:seed
make test → run backend & frontend tests





 ⚡ CI/CD (GitHub Actions)
Workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml:
1. Checkout
2. Setup PHP, Composer, Node
3. Install backend deps, run tests
4. Install frontend deps, run lint + tests
5. Start stack via dockercompose
6. Run Cypress E2E tests
7. Upload coverage results as artifacts



 DOCUMENTATION
 README.md → Overview, setup, commands, env variables, production deployment
 docs/openapi.yaml → Full OpenAPI spec
 docs/architecture.md → Data flow (Mermaid diagram)
 docs/assumptions.md → Avatar source, language, defaults
 CHANGELOG.md & CONTRIBUTING.md → Project maintenance



 ✅ ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Register API returns valid QR and sends email
2. Admin can login, accept/reject participants
3. Scanner reads QR and logs valid scan
4. Avatar displays & TTS plays correct greeting
5. Invalid QR = 403 + log entry
6. All tests pass in CI pipeline
7. Dockerized stack runs with make up
8. Documentation complete and correct
